newsitem.title: USA: U.S. House votes to privatize Sallie Mae.
newsitem.headline: U.S. House votes to privatize Sallie Mae.

text.p: The House voted Tuesday to privatize two government-sponsored enterprises, the Student Loan Marketing Association, known as Sallie Mae, and the College Construction Loan Insurance Association, known as Connie Lee. The bill was approved by voice vote and sent to the Senate.

It gives Sallie Mae shareholders the right to vote to reorganize and become a private sector company. If they did, Sallie Mae would continue to purchase student loans through September 30, 2007, when the company would cease to be a government-sponsored enterprise.
If Salle Mae stockholders voted against reorganization, Sallie Mae would have to conclude its business by July 1, 2013.
The bill also would repeal the authorizing legislation that created Connie Lee and require the federal government to sell Connie Lee stock currently owned by the Education Department.
